name: Aripiprazole
summary: A partial dopamine agonist atypical antipsychotic used in schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and as an adjunct for major depression.
mechanism: Partial agonist at D2 and 5-HT1A receptors and antagonist at 5-HT2A — stabilizes rather than abolishes dopamine tone.

dosing.adult: Schizophrenia: 10–15 mg once daily; adjunct for depression: 2–5 mg to start

safety.pregnancy: Limited data; third-trimester antipsychotic exposure can cause neonatal extrapyramidal or withdrawal symptoms.
safety.lactation: Present in breast milk; limited data.
warnings: Boxed warning (antipsychotics): increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis
Akathisia is common and can mimic agitation or anxiety
Metabolic effects — weight gain and glucose/lipid changes (less than olanzapine, but present)
Rare impulse-control disorders (e.g., pathological gambling) — FDA warning
monitoring: Mood and suicidality when used for depression
safety.overdose: Sedation, tachycardia, and EPS; generally moderate toxicity — supportive care.

indications: Adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder
clinicalPearls: Akathisia is common and can masquerade as worsening anxiety — don't 'increase the dose' until it is excluded.
Long half-life (~75 h) — several days to steady state; simple once-daily dosing.
good: Psychosis or mood disorders where minimizing sedation and metabolic burden matters.
bad: Patients bothered by akathisia, or with impulse-control vulnerability (rare gambling warning).
